chunks: It was narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performs hajj with debt, while he has already performed the Hajj of Islam. He said: "Yes. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will settle it on his behalf, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills."

key_terms.إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: if Allah, Exalted is He, wills
key_terms.بِدَيْنٍ: by means of debt or borrowed liability
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory Hajj incumbent in Islam

ai.seo_question: Can someone who already performed the obligatory Hajj go for hajj again using borrowed money?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the case of a person who has already fulfilled the obligatory Hajj and then undertakes another hajj while relying on debt. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits it and expresses hope in Allah’s aid in the repayment of that debt. The report reflects both a legal ruling concerning supererogatory hajj and trust in Allah’s provision.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2901 - It was narrated from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who performs Hajj with borrowed money and has already performed the Hajj of Islam.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, and Allah (swt), the Exalted, will settle his debt, God willing."
